blocks.text: Expose semantic choices to feature code and keep ownership mechanics private. A caller describes the feedback; it does not select an ARIA role, create a timeout, or manipulate the portal.

steps.title: Describe the outcome
steps.text: Feature code calls toast.success('Profile saved', { dedupeKey: 'profile-save:42', lifetime: { kind: 'timed' } }). For a conflict it supplies a Review action and persistent lifetime.

steps.title: Normalize once
steps.text: The API resolves provider defaults, validates that an action cannot inherit timed expiry, registers the action command, and sends one add command with a stable toast ID to the store.

steps.title: Render derived state
steps.text: The viewport subscribes to visible records and renders buttons whose handlers send action or dismiss intent. It never copies records into local component state and never calls setTimeout.

steps.title: Remove through one gate
steps.text: Both dismiss(id) and the lifecycle coordinator’s expiry signal reach the same remove operation. The accepted transition disposes runtime before publishing the new store snapshot; a second signal for that ID returns unchanged.

blocks.title: Contract decisions
columns: Why it is visible in the API
rows: The caller can update progress or dismiss one known result without searching by message text.
Use lifetime instead of raw milliseconds alone
Persistent is an explicit semantic state, not a special duration value.
The announcer maps ordinary status to polite speech and reserves interruption for urgent outcomes.
The application configures one viewport policy instead of allowing each caller to compete for space.

blocks.title: Action failure
blocks.text: While Review or Undo runs, update the same toast to pending and disable repeat activation. On failure, keep the persistent record visible with retry text. On success, update or dismiss it through the same ID; the domain operation, not the toast, decides whether recovery succeeded.
